gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-gafata: Gafata is contemporary and wide-eyed, its lowercase e opening up beneath short stalks above a deep band of letters. Plakkaat, heavy and drawn like a bent straw, belongs up large on just a few words.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-inter-tight: Heavy and bold, Plakkaat sweeps its terminals round until they almost meet the stem. Inter Tight is modern and open, with short ascenders and curve tails held well back from the body.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-khula: Plakkaat looks bent from a single heavy wire. Khula holds its curves open and swells through the midsection, so the uniform wire of the heading and the brushy body sit clearly apart.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-liter: Liter keeps its strokes free of contrast, with a lowercase that stands up strongly and round forms opening wide. Liter would carry paragraphs smoothly, modern and open, a foil for the closed, heavy Plakkaat above.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-michroma: Michroma reads contemporary and widely spaced, each letter given a wide berth with curves leaving daylight between their ends. And Michroma wants a modest size bump, since its stubby ascenders and wide spacing sit against the Plakkaat heading.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Heavy lettering, closed up tight and plainly bold. Noto Sans Adlam reads clean and contemporary, with curve endings kept well apart, so longer paragraphs under Plakkaat would flow without clutter.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-adlam-u: Heavy letters that look cut from wire. Noto Sans Adlam Unjoined gives Plakkaat its opposite, with generous space between curve ends and the stem, and almost no height gap between cases.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-anatoli: Heavy and bold, with terminals curling back toward the stem. Plakkaat hits hardest in its closed, dense forms, while Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs does its job with outward-pointing tips and a lowercase rising near cap height.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-armenia: Noto Sans Armenian reads approachable and professional, its round letters opening wide and its lowercase standing full and confident. Whole paragraphs would stay inviting beneath the closed, heavy Plakkaat headline.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-avestan: Heavy and bold, Plakkaat curls its terminals shut. Noto Sans Avestan is the open-handed opposite, curve tips never touching and an x-height that stands out, and that gap defines the pairing.
